ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An ideal gas of a certain mass undergoes an isobaric process from $A$ to $B$, followed by an adiabatic process from $B$ to $C$ (no heat exchange between the gas and the surroundings), during which the internal energy decreases by 900 J.

1. Determine the total work done by the gas on the surroundings during the entire process from $A$ to $B$ to $C$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An ideal gas of a certain mass undergoes an isobaric process from $A$ to $B$, followed by an adiabatic process from $B$ to $C$ (no heat exchange between the gas and the surroundings), during which the internal energy decreases by 900 J. 1. Determine the total work done by the gas on the surroundings during the entire process from $A$ to $B$ to $C$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a p-V graph, with the vertical axis labeled p/10^5 Pa and the horizontal axis labeled V/10^-3 m^3. Point A is located at V=2×10^-3 m^3, p=6×10^5 Pa; point B is located at V=3×10^-3 m^3, p=6×10^5 Pa. From A to B is a horizontal rightward isobaric expansion process; from B to C is a process curving toward the lower right. Reasoning: A→B is an isobaric process, and the work done by the gas on the outside is W_AB=p(V_B−V_A)=6×10^5×(3×10^-3−2×10^-3)=600 J. B→C is an adiabatic process, Q_BC=0; the problem gives that the internal energy decreases by 900 J, that is, ΔU_BC=-900 J. Using the first law of thermodynamics ΔU=Q−W_by_gas, then -900=0−W_BC, so W_BC=900 J. The total work done by the gas on the outside in the whole process is W_total=W_AB+W_BC=600+900=1500 J.
